title: India Joins US and 24 Nations in Global Alliance to Shape 6G Networks
excerpt: The agreement, finalised at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in North Carolina, commits participating countries to cooperate on security, interoperability and AI integration in next-generation telecoms.
body:
• India has joined the US-led Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, an alliance of 26 nations shaping next-generation telecom standards
  • The agreement was finalised after US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick met India's Minister of State for Commerce Jitin Prasada at the G20 Innovation Ministerial
  • The alliance's agenda includes network security, interoperability, resilience and the role of trusted AI in 6G infrastructure
  • India is simultaneously pursuing its own Bharat 6G Mission to become a global hub for 6G intellectual property and cost-effective telecom solutions

India Enters the 6G Race

India has joined the United States and 24 other nations in an international initiative to guide the development and deployment of next-generation 6G telecommunications networks, the US Department of Commerce announced on Monday.

The agreement was finalised following a bilateral meeting between US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, held on September 1-2.

"Today, we are pleased to announce that India has joined the U.S. and 24 other countries in the effort to ensure that next generation networks reflect our shared security interests, strengthen our competitiveness, and drive innovation in 6G."

— US Department of Commerce

What the Alliance Covers

Under the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, launched by the US Department of Commerce's National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), participating countries have pledged to strengthen cooperation on 6G over the next 12 months and beyond.

The alliance's agenda spans network security, interoperability, resilience and the role of trusted artificial intelligence in the development and operation of 6G infrastructure. The initiative is also meant to ensure that 6G standards reflect the security interests of democratic nations — a pointed signal in the context of ongoing US-China technology competition.

During the bilateral meeting, India and the US also discussed strengthening cooperation in semiconductors, AI and data centres. Prasada encouraged the possibility of more US investments in India's semiconductor mission (ISM 2.0) and proposed strengthening the AI technology partnership.

India's Domestic 6G Ambitions

India is not simply joining an American-led effort. The country is independently pursuing its own 6G ambitions through the Bharat 6G Mission, which aims to make India a global hub for 6G intellectual property, products and cost-effective telecom solutions.

India's telecom trajectory has been remarkable. The country leapfrogged from limited 3G coverage to becoming the world's largest consumer of mobile data under 4G, then executed one of the fastest 5G rollouts globally. The Bharat 6G Mission seeks to ensure India is not just a consumer of next-generation technology but a creator and standard-setter.

The G20 Innovation Ministerial concluded with a joint statement recognising that emerging technologies have the potential to "unlock prosperity, enhance productivity, and expand opportunity." India reaffirmed its commitment to building strategic partnerships in AI, semiconductors, digital public infrastructure, robotics and other emerging technologies.

What It Means for Tech Professionals

For Indian tech professionals and diaspora workers in the telecoms and semiconductor sectors, the alliance signals growing demand for 6G research and development talent across both India and the US. As the two countries deepen cooperation on standards-setting and infrastructure deployment, opportunities are likely to expand in areas like network architecture, AI-driven network management and edge computing.

India's push for cost-effective 6G solutions could also benefit developing nations that have relied on affordable Indian telecom infrastructure — extending the model that made Jio's 4G revolution a case study in emerging-market connectivity.

What's Next

Alliance members have committed to concrete cooperation within the next 12 months. India's participation in both the US-led initiative and its own Bharat 6G Mission positions it to play a dual role — as a standards-setter in the global alliance and as a developer of indigenous 6G technology for domestic and export markets.
